h: Salvation and Teshuvah Clothe the Soul in Light

p: "'I will greatly rejoice' — over the evil inclination,
which is uprooted from the midst of Yisrael;
'my soul shall exult in my God'
This is what it says in the haftarah:
"For He has clothed me in garments of salvation."
which is a garment for the soul.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּזֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב עו, א)
And as written in the holy Zohar (Zohar II 76a),
that the essence of man is the soul,
and the body is called only "the flesh of man."
"You clothed me with skin and flesh,"
for it is only a garment.
And at first, before the sin,
there were "garments of light" with an alef,
and afterward they became "garments of skin" with an ayin,
which is the skin of the serpent
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּתִּיקּוּנִים הַקְדָּמָה דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל וְעוֹד)
(as written in the Tikkunim, Introduction, the passage beginning "Ve'od").
And the main salvation a person needs
is salvation from the evil inclination.
And this is what it says:
"For He has clothed me in garments of salvation":
that is, that the evil inclination is uprooted
and according to what is written
it is said of the Ancient of Days."
And at the third meal of Shabbos,
when there is the revelation of the Forehead of Atika,
For the main intent of Amalek
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּזֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (שָׁם קס, א)
as written in the holy Zohar (Zohar III 160a):
this is the evil inclination," etc.
And Amalek is the kelipah of the dog,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּזֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב סה, א)
as written in the holy Zohar (Zohar II 65a),
of the ox and the donkey,
which are the kelipos of Esav and Yishmael;
have the numerical value of kelev (dog).
at the revelation of the Forehead of Atika,
we say, "They are carried outside," etc.,
for then already "I will greatly rejoice" over the evil inclination,
which is uprooted from the midst of Yisrael.
"He has wrapped me in a robe of righteousness"
"my soul shall exult in my God,"
of which the Pesikta cited above says:
and the hei indicates the upper hei,
through which deliberate sins become for him like merits,
And this is the meaning of "a robe of righteousness":
that from the sins is made
a garment of light and merits.
And it is along the lines of what we said is the meaning of
וְהוֹתִירְךָ ה׳ בְּכֹל מַעֲשֵׂה יָדְךָ לְטוֹבָה
"And Hashem will give you abundance in all the work of your hands, for good":
that from all the deeds he did
there will remain an advantage for good,
And this is what it says,
"and my soul shall exult in my God":
that the soul, which is the essence of man,
will rejoice in being wrapped in a robe of righteousness,
that there will remain an advantage for good,
that he will merit the higher teshuvah,
and that they will become like merits.
כִּי כָאָרֶץ תּוֹצִיא צִמְחָהּ (יְשַׁעְיָה סא, יא)
"For as the earth brings forth its growth" (Yeshayahu 61:11):
this is what grows without sowing;
"and as a garden makes its seeds sprout":
"so will Hashem God cause righteousness to sprout."
עַל יְדֵי מַה שֶּׁגָּלוּי וְיָדוּעַ לְפָנֶיךָ
through "it is revealed and known before You
that our will is to do Your will,"
that is, that at the root
they are bound to Hashem Yisbarach.
וְיֵשׁ אוֹר זָרוּעַ לַצַּדִּיק (תְּהִלִּים צז, יא)
And there is "light sown for the tzaddik" (Tehillim 97:11),
for Hashem Yisbarach sowed this light
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (בְּזֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ חֵלֶק ב קסו, ב)
as written (in the holy Zohar, Zohar II 166b).

inlineHeadings.text: The Body Saved From the Yetzer Hara
The Past Becomes a Robe of Righteousness

paragraphs.text: Source: Yeshayahu 61:10 — “שוש אשיש ביהוה תגל נפשי באלהי כי הלבישני בגדי ישע מעיל צדקה יעטני כחתן יכהן פאר וככלה תעדה כליה” — “I greatly rejoice in GOD, My whole being exults in my God—Who has clothed me with garments of triumph, Wrapped me in a robe of victory, Like a bridegroom adorned with a turban, Like a bride bedecked with her finery.”
